The test image shows a corn leaf with a large, irregular grayish-white/silver lesion with a shiny wet appearance, dark spots at the lesion margins, and wavy/irregular edges. This strongly suggests **Goss_wilt** (freckles + shiny exudate) or possibly **Stewarts_wilt** (wavy leaf-vein following margins).

Let me view the reference images for the top candidates.

The Goss_wilt reference (top-right panel) shows very similar large irregular water-soaked lesions. Stewarts_wilt reference shows seedlings - doesn't match. Let me check Downy_mildew and Northern_corn_leaf_blight to rule them out.

Downy mildew shows pale chlorotic seedlings — doesn't match. NCLB shows cigar-shaped lesions — too regular. The test image is clearly not these.

Let me view two more references to complete my budget minimum.

Gray_leaf_spot shows small rectangular parallel-edged lesions — doesn't match. Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight shows small tan rectangular spots — doesn't match.

**Summary of visual evidence:**
- Very large, irregular-shaped grayish-silver lesion covering much of the upper leaf
- Shiny, wet/glistening appearance consistent with bacterial exudate
- Dark spots/freckles visible at lesion margins
- Wavy, irregular margins (not constrained to leaf veins in a regular way)
- Water-soaked appearance

This matches **Goss_wilt** precisely: "Large, water-soaked lesions with very irregular shapes, dark spots or 'freckles' at lesion margins, and shiny bacterial exudate on the leaf surface." The Goss_wilt reference collage (top-right panel) showed identical irregular large water-soaked lesions. No other candidate fits — Gray_leaf_spot/NCLB/SCLB all have well-defined, smaller, regularly-shaped lesions; Stewarts_wilt shows streaky yellow/pale symptoms following veins without the large silver blotch pattern.
